findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project ids
findings.body: The key is built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's tuple hash is not guaranteed unique, so two different project sets can collide and share a cached eligibility result. A non-allowlisted project set could then be upsampled, or the reverse. The hash is also not a stable cache key. Use the joined project ids instead.

findings.title: Cache invalidation is never called
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing calls it, for example when the allowlist option changes. Allowlist changes are therefore stale for up to 60 seconds. Because the key is per project set, invalidating after an option change is impractical anyway. The 60s cache saves almost nothing, since options.get is already cheap and cached.

findings.title: Transform emits 'upsampled_count() as count', which is only defined in the discover dataset
findings.body: The transform runs for the errors dataset and for the RPC/other paths, but upsampled_count is only registered in the discover dataset function converter. The errors dataset or its builder may not know the function, so such queries can fail. The transform is also applied to the discover queries run in the widget-split paths. The "as count" alias with the string-based parser is unverified.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: The check passes the closed-over `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` argument. In the dashboard split paths the queried dataset is `discover` or the scoped one, so the decision is made against the wrong dataset. It also reads `event.type:error` from the request query rather than the `query` argument. The split path appends `AND !event.type:transaction`, so the actual query is not what gets checked. The check also runs on every call, including the repeated split queries.

findings.title: upsampled_count assumes a sample_weight column and sums NULLs
findings.body: sum(sample_weight) returns NULL or 0 for events that have no sample_weight, so counts drop to 0 for those events. The code comments assume the column exists for all events, but nothing enforces that. A fallback such as a coalesce to 1 is missing. The function is also registered without the `private` flag, so users can call it directly in discover queries.

findings.title: Test factory silently swallows exceptions and sets sample_rate on every event
findings.body: The helper uses broad `except Exception: pass` blocks. It also changes `sample_rate` for every stored event in the shared test factory. A falsy rate of 0 is ignored. This can affect unrelated tests.

findings.title: Tests don't cover top_events, the RPC path, or the cache
findings.body: The upsampling tests mock `options` and cover only the plain timeseries path. They do not cover topEvents or the cache hit/miss behavior. The sorted-vs-cached eligibility interaction is also untested. The test setUp reassigns self.user after login, which is confusing.

findings.title: Stray submodule/gitlink file added
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` subproject commit entry was added accidentally. It should not be part of this PR.
